title: The smooth dualizing object is the Tate twist
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, in the domain of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure relative dimension $d$. With the coefficient twists of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed], there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

proof.text: Work at the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ prescribed by [def-pur-conventions]. Choose a finite affine open cover $\{V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i\}$ of $Y$ with each $B_i$ finitely generated over $k$, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X_i=X\times_YV_i$, $f_i:X_i\to V_i$, $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, and $W_i=X_i\times_{V_i}X_i$. The domain of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] gives that $f$ is separated and finite type. Thus [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] gives the same properties for $f_i$ and the two projections of $W_i$, and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1) gives their smoothness of pure relative dimension $d$. The affine structure map $V_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3); composing separated maps by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) makes $X_i$ and $W_i$ separated over $k$. They are finite type over $k$: a finite affine cover of $X_i$ has coordinate rings finitely generated over $B_i$, hence over $k$, and the same argument applies to $W_i$ over an affine cover of $X_i$. This is the finite-type criterion in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Finally [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3) gives canonical identifications $Lj_i^*\omega_f\cong\omega_{f_i}$. All subsequent applications of the restricted DNC theorem are to these separated finite-type schemes.

source.place: Step 1, localized on affine target opens to meet the current DNC hypotheses; Stacks Tags 01S7, 01KU, 01T3, 01T4, 01VB, 02NK

proof.text: For each $i$, let $p_{1,i},p_{2,i}:W_i\to X_i$ be the projections and $\Delta_i:X_i\hookrightarrow W_i$ the diagonal. By [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] there is the canonical isomorphism $\alpha_i:C(p_{1,i},\Delta_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f_i}$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], the diagonal is a regular closed immersion of pure codimension $d$, with $N_i=N_{\Delta_i/W_i}\cong T_{X_i/V_i}$. The normal-bundle description of [def-pur-normal-bundle] makes $\pi_i:N_i\to X_i$ a vector bundle of rank $d$, with zero section $z_i$. The identity $p_{1,i}\Delta_i=\operatorname{id}_{X_i}$ verifies the section hypothesis. Step 1 verifies that both the base $X_i$ and the total space $W_i$ are separated finite type over $k$ and that $p_{1,i}$ is separated finite type and smooth of pure dimension $d$. Consequently [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] applies and gives its uniquely normalized comparison $\delta_i:C(p_{1,i},\Delta_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_i,z_i)$.

source.place: Step 1: the section invariant of the diagonal, on each separated target chart

proof.text: Apply [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] to $\pi_i$ to obtain $\omega_{\pi_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{N_i}(d)[2d]$. By [def-pur-section-invariant], $C(\pi_i,z_i)=Lz_i^*\omega_{\pi_i}$. Restricting the vector-bundle comparison to $z_i$ gives $\beta_i:C(\pi_i,z_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{X_i}(d)[2d]$. For the final identification use [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] for $z_i$, at the finite coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$: $z_i^{-1}\Lambda_{N_i}(d)\cong\Lambda_{X_i}(d)$ on the small pro-etale site. Derived finite-coefficient pullback is termwise inverse image by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], so this sheaf comparison also gives the displayed shifted comparison. The twists are those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]; at finite level their nonnegative powers are sheaves in degree zero. The same Tate comparison for open inclusions identifies $\Lambda_X(d)|_{X_i}$ with $\Lambda_{X_i}(d)$. Form the local orientation $\theta_i=\beta_i\delta_i\alpha_i^{-1}:\omega_{f_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{X_i}(d)[2d]$, and use Step 1 to view its source as $\omega_f|_{X_i}$.

source.place: Step 2: the two sides; combining the diagonal, DNC and zero-section comparisons locally

proof.text: We check agreement of these maps on overlaps, without assuming that an intersection of affine target opens is affine. Cover $V_i\cap V_j$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)_b$ distinguished in $V_i$ and contained in $V_j$. The basis assertion is [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i), and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) identifies their affine coordinate rings with the displayed localizations; $(B_i)_b$ is finitely generated over $k$, by adding $b^{-1}$ to generators of $B_i$. For $X_V=X\times_YV$, repeat Steps 1--3 and call the resulting orientation $\theta_V$. The base change of the pair $(W_i\to X_i,\Delta_i)$ along $a_i:X_V\to X_i$ is exactly $(X_V\times_VX_V\to X_V,\Delta_V)$: once the first component has image in $V$, its second component has the same image in $Y$ and therefore also lies over $V$. The same description holds using $j$. By [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3), the dualizing-object comparisons in [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] restrict to those for $f_V$. By the base-change compatibility in [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], the restriction of $\delta_i$ is $\delta_V$, with the normal bundle and zero section identified with their pullbacks. This application has separated finite-type base $X_V$ by Step 1; its morphism $a_i$ needs no flatness hypothesis. By the base-change compatibility in [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity], the zero-section comparison $\beta_i$ restricts to $\beta_V$. Thus, under the canonical source restriction and Tate target restriction identifications of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists], $\theta_i|_{X_V}=\beta_V\delta_V\alpha_V^{-1}=\theta_V=\theta_j|_{X_V}$. These equalities also hold on a further refinement, because each comparison is the pullback of the same canonical factor. The next two steps convert this local equality into equality and gluing on $X_i\cap X_j$.

source.place: Combining paragraph: base-change compatibility, used on common affine refinements of target overlaps; Stacks Tags 00E0 (basic-open basis), 01I3 (standard-open-affine)

proof.text: Here is the explicit reduction to sheaf maps on the possibly nonseparated scheme $X$. Put $K=\omega_f$, $r=-2d$, $M=\mathcal H^r(K)$ and $G=\Lambda_X(d)$, using [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1)--(3), sheaves on each open are exactly sheaves on the localized site with the restricted constant coefficient ring. Exact restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] commutes with kernels, images and quotients, hence with cohomology. The local orientations of Step 3 therefore give $\mathcal H^q(K)|_{X_i}=0$ for $q\ne r$. A sheaf which restricts to zero on a covering family is zero: restrict any section to the induced cover of its domain and apply uniqueness in the sheaf axiom. Thus $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q\ne r$ globally. For a representative $P$ of $K$, the good truncation of [def-kun-truncations] gives the explicit roof $P\xleftarrow{\sim}\tau_{\le r}P\xrightarrow{\sim}M[-r]$. The left arrow induces an identity on cohomology in degrees at most $r$, and the groups above $r$ vanish. The right arrow is the quotient $\ker d^r\to\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$ in degree $r$ and zero in lower degrees; it induces the identity in degree $r$, and the other cohomology groups vanish. Both arrows are therefore quasi-isomorphisms. Inverting the left arrow in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives the canonical isomorphism $\epsilon:K\xrightarrow{\sim}M[2d]$. Both truncation and cohomology preserve quasi-isomorphisms by their displayed cohomology computations, so the natural roof descends through the localization universal property and is independent of the representative. The roof is natural in $P$; exact restriction preserves its kernels and quotient, so it gives the same isomorphism on every open. This calculation uses no absolute separatedness and does not apply the separated-scheme concentration lemma to $X$.

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations): good truncations and the explicit kernel/quotient calculation; derived localization as in Definition 05RU

proof.text: Taking $\mathcal H^{-2d}$ of $\theta_i$ gives isomorphisms of sheaves $t_i:M|_{X_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_{X_i}$. Their restrictions to the common affine refinements agree by Step 4. Apply uniqueness in [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] on the cover of each overlap $X_i\cap X_j$ by these $X_V$ to conclude that $t_i$ and $t_j$ agree on the whole overlap. The same node, now for the covering family $\{X_i\to X\}$, glues them to a unique sheaf map $t:M\to G$. Their inverses agree as well and glue to $s:G\to M$; uniqueness applied to $st$ and $ts$ makes them the identity, so $t$ is an isomorphism. Define $\theta_f=t[2d]\circ\epsilon:K\xrightarrow{\sim}G[2d]$. After removing the common shift, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies morphisms between degree-zero sheaves with their sheaf maps, so $\theta_f|_{X_i}$ is exactly $\theta_i$, not just an isomorphism with the same source and target. For another affine cover, Step 4 gives agreement on a common affine refinement, and sheaf-map uniqueness gives the same $t$ and hence the same $\theta_f$. The factors of each $\theta_i$ are canonical, with the DNC factor fixed by its uniqueness clause in Step 2. The global map is therefore canonical and proves the asserted isomorphism for arbitrary finite-type $X,Y$ and separated smooth $f$.

The small pro-etale site of an open subscheme is the localized site, and its constant ring is the restriction of the original ring; this allows the sheaf restriction and gluing tools to apply literally.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions],
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

proof.text:
The final restriction of the Tate line uses [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with tensor identifications as in [def-weil-derived-tensor].
Step 1: the section invariant of the diagonal. Apply
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance] to the smooth map
$p_1:W\to X$ of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] and its closed
section $\Delta$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion] its
normal bundle is canonically $N_\Delta\cong T_{X/Y}$, a vector
bundle of rank $d$, so

$$
C(p_1,\Delta)\;\cong\;C(\pi_T:T_{X/Y}\to X,\,0_T).
$$

Step 2: the two sides. The left side is $\omega_f$ by
[lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. For the right side,
[cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] applied to $\pi_T$ gives

$$
\omega_{\pi_T}=R\pi_T^!\Lambda_X\;\cong\;\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d],
$$

and pulling back by the zero section $0_T$ gives

$$
C(\pi_T,0_T)=0_T^*\omega_{\pi_T}
\;\cong\;0_T^*\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d]
\;\cong\;\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

Combining the two steps proves the assertion. The identification is
canonical (every displayed step is canonical, by the uniqueness clause
of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]); compatibility with base change
follows from the base-change compatibility of the diagonal, of
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and of
[cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] (the normal bundle of the diagonal
of the base change is the base change of the normal bundle).
